methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $60M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Mitra Chem is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Vivas Kumar and Will Chueh that has raised $60M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private companies in the same sector and stage cohort, including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $60M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B to later-stage step-ups, yielding $114M. Peer-median analysis references three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The median across these three peers is $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $97M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $557M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty about whether Mitra Chem will achieve peer-level traction and scale. Key sensitivities include technology validation, path to commercial deployment, and capital efficiency relative to the comparable set. The peer-median method suggests significantly higher valuation than stage-progression, indicating substantial optionality is priced into climate-tech Series C rounds.
